g.text: The recursive result is trusted, not traced.
Work done per call or level.
The call as written, concrete args.
Half-evaluated term, as in a trace.
Parametric size, as in a recurrence.
Trace written in the program’s own syntax.
Diagram placed next to the code or rule.
Arrows tie parts of the diagram to code.
Function and parameter names reused in nodes.
Linked to an equation, not to code.
Size n aligned to size n−1.
Down to the base case, then back up.
Value written on the way back.
Dead branches, keyed in a legend.
The decision named on the edge.
Rule implied by a few levels.
Cases of one step side by side.
Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
